items.title: #432 The Mind of Napoleon
items.description:
Founder OS from Napoleon’s own maxims: speed over perfect plans, morale as a production system, and thin rule-sets that compound under pressure.
Not hustle lore — decision heuristics that scale.

items.title: #434 Sam Walton
items.description: Operator craft via Vance Trimble’s Walton bio: buy cheap, sell low, every day, with a smile — density of merchandising heuristics without the pain-lore frame.

items.title: #431 How Henry Singleton Worked
items.description:
What I learned from reading Distant Force: A Memoir of the Teledyne Corporation and The Man Who Created It by George Roberts and The Outsiders by William Thorndike — how Henry Singleton worked.

Singleton's capital allocation as operating system — aggressive buybacks as strategy, not financial-engineering cosplay.
Operator densifier: Teledyne/Outsiders playbook on how a founder-CEO compounds when the market misunderstands him.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/431-how-henry-singleton-worked/id1141877104?i=1000786905410

items.title: #430 How to Write Ads That Sell
items.description:
Claude Hopkins was the greatest copywriter of all time. His ideas were so valuable that when he wrote them down in a book the founder of his advertising firm locked the manuscript in a safe for 20 years. When the book was finally published it sold over 8 million copies. David Ogilvy said that nobody should work in advertising until they had read the book seven times. This episode is what I learned by reading Claude Hopkins' autobiography My Life In Advertising and his legendary book Scientific Advertising.

Why this sharpens your taste: Hopkins’ rule — advertising is salesmanship in print, measured by results, not cleverness. Craft move: treat every line as a testable claim; Senra extracts the operator habit behind Scientific Advertising.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/430-how-to-write-ads-that-sell/id1141877104?i=1000785306106
